thread:
anya: Heads up — after yesterday's RBAC cleanup I started seeing gaps in audit logs for KMS decrypt events. Our nightly DAST job failed to pull creds and SAST spiked a few new dependency warnings. Anyone triaging?

kevin: I noticed failures too. KMS API returns 403 for principal 'scanner-runner@redwood-prod'. Looks like kms.decrypt was removed.

sam: Did the org-level role removal accidentally remove key-level bindings? I only touched infra-reader at org scope, not key ACLs. @marie can you check the key?

marie: Confirmed — key ring binding for projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/security/cryptoKeys/scanner-key had kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter removed in PR #3124. Re-adding now.

sec-bot: Incident created SEC-2026-042: "kms-decrypt-403-scanner" assigned to sec-oncall.

anya: Two asks: 1) Can DAST be patched to retry with fallback credential so nightly doesn't silently miss runs? 2) We need to reconstruct audit evidence for the window where the decrypts failed and attach to vuln tickets.

kevin: For (1) fallback token won't help if KMS is broken — the ephemeral token is signed by the same key. We can add retry/backoff, but long-term: put a short-lived service token in Secret Manager with cross-project access (not encrypted by this single key).

marie: For (2) I can pull org-level Cloud Audit Logs + VPC flow logs + CI metadata. I'll script extraction for the gap (02:10-03:00 UTC yesterday) and upload to secure bucket with checksums. Example command I'll run: ```gcloud logging read "resource.type=kms_key AND protoPayload.methodName=Decrypt" --start-time "2025-11-12T02:10:00Z" --end-time "2025-11-12T03:00:00Z" --format json > /tmp/kms-decrypt-window.json```

anya: Thanks. Also SAST flagged a transient transitive dep after the infra change. @kevin can you re-run the SAST job locally with pinned deps before we open tickets?

kevin: Will re-run. Quick note: the scan runner lost logs.sinks.write permission as well, so some scan logs didn't get flushed to the sink. That explains partial evidence. We should give the service account logging.logWriter on the sink.

sam: I'll open a PR to re-add minimal bindings: kms.decrypt on the key for scanner-runner SA, logging.logWriter on the sink, and a narrowly-scoped infra-reader restore for the scanning SA. Also adding a pipeline unit test that validates critical service accounts keep required bindings.

marie: PR #3142 created and targets staging first. It limits decrypt to the exact service account: projects/redwood-prod/serviceAccounts/scanner-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com. Deploying canary now.

anya: Let's schedule a short blameless triage tomorrow 10:00 PT to record root cause and actions. Owners: PR gating (sam), audit alert (marie), CI retry logic (kevin), evidence script (marie).

kevin: I'll draft the blameless note and action items in the incident doc. One suggested automation: add an invariant check in the infra CI that scans diff for removal of bindings on keys and sinks and requires explicit justification label on PRs.

sam: Added that as a checklist item in the PR description. Also tagging @infra-team in the PR for awareness. :thumbsup:

marie: Once the canary succeeds, I'll run the audit extraction and attach to SEC-2026-042 with hashes.

anya: Perfect. If anyone sees additional failures from yesterday's window, add comments to the incident ticket so we have one place for evidence.

kevin: Re-run results: SAST local run shows the transitive dep is a false positive from vulnerability DB v12.4.1. I'll file a suppression with evidence instead of creating a new ticket.

sec-bot: SEC-2026-042 status updated -> mitigated (bindings restored), evidence attached by marie.

anya: Great work. Follow-ups: (A) automation in infra CI to detect key/sink binding removals, (B) fallback credential design for DAST, (C) add audit-recovery playbook to runbook. We'll cover in 15-min triage.

marie: Creating runbook PR for audit-recovery and linking to incident.

sam: I'll merge PR after staging canary passes.

kevin: Closing loop on SAST noise — suppression pushed to vuln DB team with reproducible case.

anya: Thanks team, closing thread unless new evidence pops up.
